To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dual modality instruction is not always more effective than single modality instruction, especially for L2 reading and vocabulary acquisition.

(1) dual modality input does not necessarily lead to better L2 reading comprehension and vocabulary learning outcomes than single modal input and (2) dual modality instruction may be more effective for some learners than for others.

(1) the efficacy of dual modalities in repeated reading for L2 reading and vocabulary acquisition is contingent on the instructional purpose, and (2) dual modalities are more effective for L2 learners with a visual or balanced style when the purpose is L2 reading, but more effective for L3 learners with an auditory style when the purpose of repeated reading is L2 vocabulary acquisition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
whether and how dual modality input influences L2 learning outcomes and whether the efficacy of dual mode instruction varies according to learning styles.
